hypotheses.statement: DVWA at http://127.0.0.1/ is reachable and serves the expected login page on first GET of /login.php
admin/password (DVWA default credentials) authenticates against /login.php and yields a session cookie usable for the rest of the app
DVWA's security level can be lowered to 'low' via /security.php to enable the full vulnerable-module surface

/vulnerabilities/sqli/?id=…&Submit=Submit at security=low reflects the id value verbatim into the SQL query and dumps multiple rows, allowing classic ' OR '1'='1 extraction of all users/passwords hashes
/vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/?id=…&Submit=Submit at security=low supports time-based (SLEEP) and boolean-based extraction of arbitrary data via the User-ID field
/vulnerabilities/exec/?ip=…&Submit=Submit at security=low concatenates user input directly into a shell ping command, allowing ; | & $()` command chaining for arbitrary command execution
/vulnerabilities/xss_r/?name=… at security=low reflects input unencoded into the page body, allowing <script>alert(1)</script> reflected XSS

/vulnerabilities/xss_s/?txtName=…&mtxMessage=…&btnSign=Sign+Guestbook at security=low persists the message unencoded in the database and renders it on every subsequent page load, yielding stored XSS with cookie theft potential
/vulnerabilities/fi/?page=… at security=low includes arbitrary local files via ../ traversal (e.g. page=../../../../etc/passwd) and remote files via absolute URL inclusion if allow_url_include is on
/vulnerabilities/upload/ at security=low accepts any file type (no extension/MIME validation) and stores uploads under /hackable/uploads/, enabling PHP webshell upload + execution

/vulnerabilities/csrf/ at security=low lets an authenticated admin change their password via a single GET request with no token, enabling one-click forced-password-change via cross-origin image/iframe
/vulnerabilities/brute/ at security=low forwards username/password to an unsleep()-guarded sink, allowing hydra-style high-rate brute force without lockout
/vulnerabilities/captcha/ at security=low has a CAPTCHA bypass via the documented 'step=2' two-stage flaw (changing step parameter skips validation)
/vulnerabilities/xss_d/?default=… at security=low reflects input into a JS context that is then eval'd via document.write, enabling DOM-based XSS
